methodology_note: NTA/BVPS-path model with exit P/B, discounted at COST OF EQUITY -- NOT an owner-FCF DCF and NOT an OCF-based DCF. Ryman is an ORA/DMF retirement village operator (same family as SUM.NZ): reported operating cash flow ($334m FY2026) is inflated by resident occupation-advance receipts, which are capital/financing inflows that must be continuously redeployed into new units; statutory NPAT (-$513.7m FY2025, -$171.3m FY2026) is dominated by IAS-40 fair-value movements and impairments. Unlike SUM.NZ, Ryman abandoned Underlying Profit in FY2024 and its replacement measures are currently negative (PBTF -$73.3m FY2026) or deeply depressed (Operating EBITDAF $88.3m FY2026), so the SUM-style earnings-capitalization cannot be applied to a positive earnings base. The model therefore projects book equity per share (statutory NPAT path net of dividends resuming FY2028), applies a scenario exit P/B anchored to the 10-year realised P/B history, and discounts terminal book value plus interim dividends at the cost of equity. Because the flows are post-interest and equity-level, net debt is NOT subtracted -- doing so would deduct the debt twice.

inputs.net_debt_note: Shown for reference only; NOT subtracted in the valuation (equity-level model on post-interest flows).
inputs.notes: Model: NTA/BVPS path x exit P/B at cost of equity (routed via dcf-methods: ORA/DMF operator with negative capitalizable earnings -> asset-based model, cross-checked against normalizing-earnings capitalization; consistent with the SUM.NZ principle of never discounting OCF and never double-deducting debt, but adapted because RYM is a loss-making turnaround, not a steady compounder). Shares are the post-Feb-2025-raise count of 1,015.7m; ALL per-share history before FY2025 is on a different base (500m to FY2022, 688m FY2023-24). FY2026 FCF positивe (+$112.2m OCF-capex; company measure +$188.3m) is real deleveraging progress but is still partly ORA-flow funded and is not treated as distributable owner earnings. Dividend suspended since FY2023; assumed to resume FY2028 (base/bull only) at the guided 20-50% of cash flow from existing operations. New 1.50x interest-cover covenant from Sept-2026 is the key near-term risk and is reflected in the bear weight and bear exit P/B.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue 3yr CAGR +14.4% vs equity 3yr CAGR -4.4% and BVPS 3yr CAGR -16.0%: the top line grows while fair-value losses, impairments ($243.6m FY2024, $172.9m FY2025) and the dilutive Feb-2025 raise destroyed per-share book value. EPS and FCF CAGRs are omitted: statutory EPS is IAS-40 fair-value noise (negative in FY2025-26) and reported FCF only turned positive in FY2026. Historical CAGRs computed on 1,015.7m current shares vs 500m (pre-FY2023) / 688m (FY2023-24) bases are NOT comparable per share; the equity_5yr_cagr of +7.6% includes $1.87bn of equity raises and overstates organic compounding.

base.description: Turnaround holds but housing stays sluggish: statutory NPAT recovers to breakeven FY2027 then +$120m/+$200m/+$250m/+$290m as modest fair-value gains resume on the $10.9bn book, PBTF reaches positive by FY2029 (management's $150m cash-flow improvement target partially delivered), dividends resume FY2028 at the bottom of the 20-50% CFEO range. Exit P/B 0.75x -- the FY2023 level (0.78x), i.e. turnaround credibility partly restored but ROE still below cost of equity. CoE 12.5%.

bull.description: NZ/Victoria housing recovery lifts resale margins and fair-value gains; $150m cost-out/pricing target fully delivered by FY2029; land divestments realise ~book; dividends resume FY2028 mid-range. Exit P/B 1.0x -- still below the 10yr median of 1.26x and far below the pre-crisis 2.4-2.6x. CoE 11.0% as execution premium unwinds.

bear.description: Renewed NZ/Victoria housing downturn: fair-value losses and further impairments (Australia write-downs) cut equity ~8% over FY2027-28; ICR covenant (1.50x from Sept-2026) pressures headroom and keeps dividends suspended through FY2031; no new equity raise assumed but the risk is priced in the exit multiple. Exit P/B 0.45x -- below the FY2026 realised 0.53x, a new low consistent with a broken-turnaround narrative. CoE 14.0%.

wacc_rationale: Cost of equity (NZD flows, NZD risk-free): NZ 10yr govt ~4.25% + equity risk premium 5.0% (beta ~1) = 9.25% baseline. Structural premiums charged once each: turnaround/execution risk (loss-making on PBTF, targets not yet met, repeated non-GAAP redefinitions) +1.5%; leverage against a fair-valued property book plus the 1.50x ICR covenant step-up from Sept-2026 +1.0%; residual NZ/Victoria housing-market linkage beyond what the market ERP already carries +0.75%. Base CoE = 12.5%. Bull 11.0% (execution premium halves once FY29 targets are visibly on track, rates falling); bear 14.0% (covenant stress scenario). Housing cyclicality is charged in the CoE premium only -- the bear NPAT path carries the level effect, not a second risk premium.

base.fcf_note: fcf rows are dividends paid (NZ$m) -- the only cash flow to shareholders in this model; value otherwise accrues in book equity.

entry_price.note: Entry price = PV at 15% hurdle of scenario dividends + terminal (BVPS_Y5 x exit P/B). Current $2.13 is 16% above the weighted entry of $1.83: the price only clears a 15% hurdle if the bull case plays out.
entry_price.method: PV at the 15% hurdle of the interim DIVIDENDS plus the year-5 exit value (BVPS x exit P/B), per share. VERIFIED CORRECT 2026-09-01 against the hurdle-rate rule: discounting everything at 15% reproduces the published 0.83 / 1.87 / 2.75 exactly. Unlike the FCF and capitalized-earnings engines, the exit multiple here is an explicit judgement (0.45x / 0.75x / 1.0x, argued against RYM's own P/B history) rather than a rate-derived Gordon value, so there is nothing to rebuild at the hurdle. An automated Gordon check flags this file spuriously; run_evals now skips exit-multiple models for that reason.

sensitivity.matrix_note: Intrinsic value/share (NZD), base-case NPAT and dividend path, rows = cost of equity %, cols = exit P/B. Replaces the WACC x terminal-growth grid: in this model the terminal assumption IS the exit P/B.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear held at 25% (above the house default 15%): cash generation remains hostage to the NZ/Victoria housing cycle, the 1.50x ICR covenant starts Sept-2026, and management's own non-GAAP track record (Underlying Profit abandoned, DMF accrual and cost-allocation restatements, a $77m NTA restatement) argues against giving the turnaround full credit yet. Bull at 25%: FY2026 delivered the first positive full-year FCF in a decade, Operating EBITDAF nearly doubled, debt is refinanced to FY31, and the DMF repricing (20.7% -> 30%) mechanically lifts revenue as the book turns over ~12%/yr.

sanity_check.implied_multiples_note: Implied P/E and EV/EBITDA are unavailable, not omitted: statutory EPS is negative (FY2025 -72.3c, FY2026 -16.9c) and there is no clean EBITDA series (reported EBITDA embeds IAS-40 fair-value movements; Operating EBITDAF only exists FY2024-26 and is turnaround-depressed). P/B is the meaningful check for this model.

historical_multiples.p_underlying_profit_note: Underlying Profit was abandoned by the company in FY2024; shown for历史 context only. FY-end March prices from Yahoo 10y monthly series aligned to fiscal-year rows; per-year share counts used (500m to FY2022, 688m FY2023-24, 1,015.7m FY2025+).
historical_multiples.outliers_note: FY2018-FY2021 multiples (2.4-2.6x book) belong to the pre-crisis, pre-dilution era with a 500m share base, peak housing tailwinds and an intact Underlying Profit narrative; they are kept in the table for visibility but excluded from any mean-reversion assumption -- even the bull exit P/B (1.0x) sits below the 10yr median (1.26x).

trip_detection.upside_gt_100_and_upper_half_of_range: base upside -2.0%, price in lower quarter of 10yr range -- pass

sanity_check.diagnosis: No trip. The model was routed away from the two known failure modes for this business family up front: (1) discounting OCF (inflated ~3x by ORA occupation-advance receipts -- the exact error that produced SUM.NZ's earlier $38.69/263%-upside artifact) and (2) capitalizing statutory NPAT (IAS-40 fair-value noise, currently a -$171m loss).

normalized_earnings_cross_check.method: Mature-state distributable-earnings capitalization: FY2029 Operating EBITDAF ~$238m (FY2026 $88.3m + full $150m improvement target) less net interest ~$78m less D&A ~$43m = ~$117m distributable proxy (minimal cash tax under the ORA/DMF structure); capitalized at CoE 12.5% less 2% growth = $1,117m at FY2029; PV ~$785m = $0.77/share.
normalized_earnings_cross_check.interpretation: The operating flows ALONE (excluding all fair-value/DMF embedded-value growth on the $10.9bn property book) support only ~$0.77/share, while stated NTA is ~$4.01. The base IV of $2.09 (0.52x book) sits between these bounds -- which is exactly what the market is pricing at 0.53x book: the equity is a levered residual whose value depends on how much of the revaluation engine restarts. This wide bound is why the NTA x realised-exit-P/B model is primary and any pure earnings capitalization (which spans $0.77 to $3.50+ depending on the earnings concept chosen) is only a cross-check.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Ryman at $2.13 trades at 0.53x book -- against a 10-year P/B range of 0.53x-2.64x and a post-crisis (FY2023-26) range of 0.53x-0.78x. This is a loss-making turnaround, not a compounder: statutory NPAT is negative (fair-value losses and impairments), PBTF is -$73m, Underlying Profit no longer exists, and the dividend has been suspended since FY2023. The model therefore values the equity as a levered residual on a $10.9bn fair-valued property book: project book value per share under three NPAT paths, apply an exit P/B the market has actually paid (bear 0.45x / base 0.75x / bull 1.00x -- the bull case is still below the 10yr median of 1.26x and nowhere near the old 2-3x premium, which belonged to a different company with a 500m share base and an intact growth story), and discount at cost of equity. Weighted IV $2.08 vs price $2.13: the market is pricing the turnaround roughly fairly. The stock only clears a 15% hurdle at ~$1.83, and the payoff is asymmetric around execution -- bull $3.27 (+53%) if the FY29 cash targets land and dividends resume FY2028, bear $0.86 (-60%) if housing rolls over into the Sept-2026 covenant step-up. Deliberate deviation from the SUM.NZ precedent (Underlying-Profit capitalization): SUM has a positive, growing, management-endorsed earnings measure; RYM abandoned its equivalent and its replacements are negative or depressed, so an earnings capitalization has no defensible base year here.
key_choices: Model: BVPS path x exit P/B at cost of equity (no net-debt subtraction -- equity-level, post-interest).
Never discount OCF for an ORA/DMF operator (capital inflows, not owner earnings).
Exit P/B anchored to realised history, not the pre-crisis premium; even bull (1.0x) < 10yr median (1.26x).
Bear weight 25% for the housing/covenant/credibility triad; bull 25% for genuine FY2026 delivery.
Cross-checked against normalizing-earnings capitalization ($0.77/share, operating flows only) and stated NTA ($4.01) -- IV sits between the bounds, as does the market price.
